newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Peso scare sends Manila stocks down at close.
newsitem.headline: Peso scare sends Manila stocks down at close.

text.p: Manila stocks fell sharply on Tuesday due to rising fears over the volatility of the foreign exchange market, traders said.
The main index fell 54.49 points, or by 1.98 percent, to 2,698.66.
"The pressure on the peso is spilling over into the equities market," said Harry Liu, president at Summit Securities.
"Everybody's scared after the rise in overnight interest rates to 30 percent."
On Monday, the Central Bank raised its overnight borrowing rate to 30 percent from 24 percent to fend off fresh speculation on the peso.
Traders said some investors unloaded their stocks on Tuesday to shift to fixed-income securities which fetched higher rates.
The bearish sentiment was exacerbated by the strike in Philippine National Bank, sending its shares lower by 11 pesos to 165.
But some issues bucked the trend. Empire East Land Holdings rose 35 centavos to 4.55 pesos on buy-in talks, which the company said it was not aware of.
Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co gained 15 pesos to 915 following the $1 1/2 rise of its ADRs in New York.
